title: 1km570e
Mu'awiya's power: kingship, Ziyad, Hujr and Yazid's succession
hook: In Mu'awiya's years the caliphate turned into kingship; Imam Ali was cursed and Yazid became crown prince.
scenes.0.text: The Prophet had foretold that the caliphate would last thirty years and then turn into a biting kingdom. It is told that **Mu'awiya** said, "I am the first of the kings." While the caliphate was a trust, he made it his own property. Under this sultanate the right of the ==Ahl al-Bayt== was not recognized.
scenes.1.text: **Mu'awiya** had the Green Palace, al-Khadra, built in Damascus. **Abu Dharr al-Ghifari** said to him: "If this is from God's wealth, it is treachery; if it is from your own wealth, it is waste." This saying is read in al-Baladhuri's Ansab al-Ashraf. Mu'awiya fell silent. Then Abu Dharr was complained about. He was expelled from Syria. He died alone at Rabadha. He was no beggar. He was a Companion who spoke the truth.
scenes.2.text: **Mu'awiya** adopted **Ziyad** as a brother, as the son of Abu Sufyan. This is called istilhaq. The Prophet's saying "the child belongs to the bed's owner" was trampled. He fabricated this lineage for power. **Ziyad** was unleashed on those who loved **Imam Ali** in Kufa and Basra. This brotherhood was made a tool of that oppression.
scenes.3.text: In the Friday sermons, from the pulpit, **Imam Ali** was made to be ==cursed==. There the Prophet's brother was reviled. **Mu'awiya** asked Sa'd why he did not curse. It is told that he wrote to the governors to curse and to punish those who loved him. This oppression lasted until Umar b. Abd al-Aziz. Love for the ==Ahl al-Bayt== was counted a crime in those years.
scenes.4.text: **Hujr b. Adi** was **Imam Ali**'s brave commander. He refused the cursing. **Ziyad** sent him with some twelve companions to Damascus. In 51 AH ==they were slaughtered at Marj Adhra.== Hujr prayed two rak'as and regarded himself as a martyr. **Mu'awiya** defended this blood. The head of Amr b. al-Hamiq was carried between cities. The cursing from the pulpit reached these killings.
scenes.5.text: **Mu'awiya** made his son **Yazid** crown prince by force. The crown prince is the son who will be ruler after him. The caliphate became a property passing from father to son. The word given with **Imam Hasan**, "I will not appoint a caliph after myself," was also trampled. In Medina **Imam Husayn** did not bow to this oppression. Abdullah b. Umar, Ibn al-Zubayr and Abd al-Rahman b. Abi Bakr were also not content. He imposed the throne on the community by force for a son.
scenes.6.text: **Yazid** is remembered for drinking wine, for amusing himself with hunting dogs and monkeys, for depravity and immorality. This accusation by the people of Medina is related in the histories. **Imam Husayn** did not give this allegiance. Allegiance is a pledge of loyalty. Giving this allegiance meant making the Prophet's grandson bow to that sultanate. Karbala is the result of this succession.
scenes.7.text: In Rajab 60 **Mu'awiya** died. The throne was left to **Yazid**. The governor of Medina demanded allegiance from **Imam Husayn**. He did not give this allegiance. He set out. He did not sell the right for a drunkard's sultanate. Karbala is the martyrdom at the end of this road. The father had established this order. The son cut off the water there.
scenes.8.text: In those years there were also those who called him a Companion and a jurist. Meanwhile the pulpit was cursing **Imam Ali**. **Hujr**'s blood was at Marj Adhra. **Ziyad** had been called brother. **Yazid** had been made crown prince. The Shia reading reads these years not as a virtue but as the oppression leading to Karbala.
sunni.0.says: The hadith «The caliphate is thirty years, then it will be kingship».
sunni.1.says: Another report of the same hadith.
sunni.2.says: Mu'awiya asking Sa'd b. Abi Waqqas why he did not curse Imam Ali.
sunni.3.says: Abd al-Rahman b. Abi Bakr's objection to the allegiance to Yazid.
sunni.4.says: Ibn Abbas's saying about Mu'awiya, «he is a jurist».
sunni.5.says: The events of 51 AH, Ziyad being declared Mu'awiya's brother, and Yazid's succession.
shia.0.says: Mu'awiya ordering his governors to have Imam Ali cursed; relayed from al-Mada'ini.
shia.1.says: Mu'awiya's power, Hujr b. Adi, and Yazid's succession.
shia.2.says: Mu'awiya has al-Khadra built in Damascus. Abu Dharr says, if it is from God's wealth, it is treachery, if from his own wealth, it is waste. Mu'awiya falls silent.
disputes.0.title: 1jy4ts
Did the caliphate turn into kingship?
disputes.0.sunni: It is agreed that Mu'awiya took over the government after 41 AH. In the Sunni reading he is a caliph; his rule is counted as an ijtihad and as peace.
disputes.0.shia: It is agreed that Mu'awiya took over the government after 41 AH. In the Shia account the succession, the istilhaq and the cursing show that the caliphate turned into inheritance and force.
disputes.1.title: 1ul0hv9
Responsibility for the killing of Hujr
disputes.1.sunni: That Hujr was killed at Marj Adhra is told in the sources. Who held the order is debated; many Sunni scholars regard this killing as a mistake.
disputes.1.shia: That Hujr was killed at Marj Adhra is told in the sources. In the Shia account this is a punishment given for his refusal to curse Imam Ali.
questions.0: The report that the caliphate would last thirty years, and the succession that followed, make you think of this rule by what name?
questions.1: The cursing of Imam Ali from the pulpit and the killing of those who refused it: what do they tell you with regard to love for the Ahl al-Bayt?
questions.2: Imam Husayn and Abd al-Rahman b. Abi Bakr were not content with Yazid's succession. What does their stand teach you in the face of an order that forces allegiance?
summary: After 41 AH Mu'awiya established a Damascus-centered rule. He declared Ziyad his brother. Imam Ali was cursed in the sermons. Hujr b. Adi was killed and his son Yazid became crown prince. In Sunni books Mu'awiya is also remembered as a Companion and a ruler. In the Shia account these years prepared the road to Karbala.
key: From caliphate to kingdom: Hujr, Ziyad and Yazid's succession
notes.0: Abu Dharr said to Mu'awiya about the Khadra Palace, 'if it is God's wealth, it is treachery, if it is your own wealth, it is waste.' He was expelled from Syria and died alone at Rabadha.
notes.1: The hadith «caliphate thirty years, then kingship» appears in Tirmidhi 2226 and Abu Dawud 4646.
notes.2: Mu'awiya declared Ziyad b. Abihi his brother (istilhaq, 44 AH).
notes.3: Cursing Imam Ali from the pulpits became an established practice.
notes.4: Hujr b. Adi was killed at Marj Adhra in 51 AH because he refused the cursing.
notes.5: He declared his son Yazid crown prince; Mu'awiya died in 60 AH and the process leading to Karbala began.
